newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen range-bound in short-term.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen range-bound in short-term.

text.p: German shares were seen moving little in late trade on Thursday and expected to take their lead on Friday morning from further developments in the dollar and on Wall Street overnight.

The IBIS DAX was trading the middle of the day's range late on Thursday at 2,769.44, 3.36 points up on the day, with dealers saying that U.S. money supply figures, due after the market close, could be the next impetus.
"They could be a focus. I don't see any real factors moving the market before then," said one trader. December DAX futures were trading five points higher at 2,775.0.
Dealers said the lower dollar and the higher start to Wall Street exerted a two-way pull on German shares that made significant movement in either direction limited.
The dollar traded at 1.4989/96, just below the key 1.500 level, while the Dow Jones index opened marginally higher.
Steel-maker Thyssen was among the most significant losers, down 5.70 marks to 275.30 in IBIS trade on concern over the publication of 1995/96 results on Friday.
The stock had recently been climbing on speculation that the firm would soon restructure.
